name: Raw honey / bee pollen

lead: Raw honey is honey that has not been heated or pasteurised, and bee pollen is the pollen pellets bees collect as food. In wellness and looksmaxxing circles both are used for clearer skin, energy and testosterone.

The chain is that honey has antibacterial activity that varies between honeys, and bee pollen supplies sugars, protein, minerals and vitamins. Honey has preliminary evidence for faster healing of some wounds and burns. Wikipedia describes bee pollen's health benefits as unproven, and no published trial was found testing either product for skin appearance or testosterone in healthy people.

paras: Honey is eaten by the spoonful, stirred into drinks or applied to skin as a mask; bee pollen granules are sprinkled on yogurt or smoothies. Users typically add them to a daily routine and report on skin over weeks.

Bee pollen can cause allergic reactions in people allergic to pollen, from hives to anaphylaxis, may be contaminated with mycotoxins, pesticides or metals, and is not considered safe in pregnancy. Honey can carry Clostridium botulinum spores and is not recommended for infants under one year. The FDA has warned about bee pollen products adulterated with unapproved drugs.

angle.text: Raw honey and bee pollen are used for clearer skin and for testosterone, on the idea that their nutrients and antibacterial properties help. Honey has some wound-care evidence; no trials test either product for appearance.

lead: Raw honey is honey taken from the hive and extracted, settled or strained without added heat, so it may retain some pollen and wax particles [1]. Bee pollen is the ball of flower pollen that worker honeybees pack and use as the hive's main food, mixed with nectar and salivary secretions [2].

Both are promoted in wellness and looksmaxxing communities for skin, energy and testosterone. Honey is mostly fructose and glucose, with a pH averaging about 3.9, and is reported to have broad antibacterial activity [1]. Bee pollen composition is variable, with about 40 to 60 percent simple sugars and 20 to 60 percent protein by one estimate [2].

For honey, preliminary evidence suggests faster healing of partial-thickness burns and moderate evidence for some post-operative wounds, while evidence for other uses is low quality or inconclusive [1]. Wikipedia describes bee pollen's health benefits as yet unproven [2]. No published trial was found testing either product for skin appearance or testosterone in healthy people.
infobox: Mostly fructose and glucose, about 15.5 to 18% water [1]
Variable; roughly 40 to 60% sugars, 20 to 60% protein [2]

paras: Honey is a supersaturated sugar solution whose high sugar content and acidity keep most microbes from growing. Raw honey is not heated, whereas pasteurisation at 72 C or higher destroys yeast but can increase hydroxymethylfurfural and reduce enzyme activity [1].

Wikipedia reports preliminary evidence that honey helps partial-thickness burns heal 4 to 5 days faster than other dressings, and moderate evidence for faster healing of post-operative infections. Evidence for other wounds is low quality, and the FDA has approved some medical-grade honey products for minor wounds and burns [1]. A Cochrane review found no strong evidence for or against honey for cough, and evidence for allergy relief is inconclusive [1]. Honey is not a cancer treatment [1].

Infants can develop botulism from honey containing Clostridium botulinum spores, and honey is not recommended before age one [1]. Honey is also sometimes adulterated with corn syrup or other sugars, and no single method detects all forms of adulteration [1].

Bee pollen's composition varies with the plants foragers visit and with time and location, so no two samples are identical [2]. Wikipedia describes the health benefits marketed for it as yet unproven and notes that scientists cited by WebMD cannot confirm that it has health benefits [2].

It is considered safe for short-term use by most people, but people with pollen allergies may experience shortness of breath, hives, swelling or anaphylaxis, and contamination by mycotoxins, pesticides or toxic metals is a risk. It is not considered safe in pregnancy and should be avoided while breastfeeding [2]. The FDA warned consumers about certain bee pollen products, including a Zi Xiu Tang capsule product in 2012 and 2014, because they were adulterated with unapproved drugs sibutramine and phenolphthalein [2].

Honey is discussed as a skin food and as a topical, and bee products are sometimes claimed to support testosterone and energy. Wikipedia's honey article covers skin only in relation to wounds and burns, and does not report evidence for testosterone [1]. These claims have not been tested in published trials of healthy people.

No studies found. No published human trial was found testing raw honey or bee pollen for skin appearance or testosterone in healthy people. Related clinical research on medical honey dressings for wounds and burns exists, and is summarised on Wikipedia [1].

timeline.event: FDA issues a notice about a bee pollen capsule product adulterated with unapproved drugs; a further notice follows in 2014 [2].
